title: Unconditional quantum advantage with noisy planar architectures
authors: Libor Caha, Robert Koenig, Louis Paletta
abstract: We consider quantum devices restricted to local operations in 2D and subject to local stochastic noise below a constant threshold. We show that such circuits are computationally more powerful than AC0-circuits, i.e., noise-free, geometrically-unconstrained constant-depth classical circuits with unbounded fan-in AND, OR and NOT gates. To this end, we exhibit a computational problem with the following properties: (i) Any instance of the problem is correctly solved with high probability by a certain geometrically 2D-local quantum circuit even if the latter is imperfectly implemented, but (ii) any polynomial-size AC0-circuit fails to solve certain instances of the problem with constant probability. To our knowledge, this isthe first complexity-theoretic separation which applies to planar quantum devices, incorporates noise-resilience and is unconditional, i.e., does not rely on complexity-theoretic assumptions. This brings the experimental demonstration of an unconditional quantum advantage closer to experimental realities.
summary: This paper proves an unconditional quantum advantage for planar quantum devices by showing that shallow, 2D-local quantum circuits can solve problems intractable for classical AC0 circuits, even when the circuits are imperfectly implemented with local noise. The authors achieve this by compiling a fault-tolerant 1D circuit into a 2D structure and demonstrating the resulting computational separation.
main_problem: To establish an unconditional quantum advantage by demonstrating that shallow, 2D-local quantum circuits are computationally more powerful than classical AC0 circuits, even when subject to realistic local stochastic noise.
main_result: The authors prove a complexity separation showing that a specific relation problem can be solved with high probability by a noisy 2D quantum circuit, while any AC0 circuit solving it must have exponentially large size.
method: The proof involves constructing a classically hard relation $R_n$ and showing that the quantum circuit solves it with high probability under noise, while the classical simulation requires an exponentially large circuit size.
model_or_system: The model considers quantum devices restricted to local operations in 2D and subject to local stochastic Pauli noise below a constant threshold. The quantum computation is compiled from a 1D-local Clifford circuit into a non-adaptive, 2D-local, constant-depth circuit.
key_observables: Success probability of the quantum circuit (high probability) versus the failure probability of the classical circuit (constant probability).
important_parameters: The noise strength must remain below a constant fault-tolerance threshold ($p_{th}$); the depth $D$ is constant, and the locality is 2D.
main_assumptions: The advantage is unconditional, meaning it does not rely on unproven complexity assumptions, but it requires the noise to be below a specific fault-tolerance threshold.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the process of compiling a 1D-local circuit into a 2D plane using gate teleportation, showing how the circuit unfolds in the (x, y) plane.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the physical model (2D, noisy, local). It then details the compilation process (1D $	o$ 2D, fault-tolerant) and the post-processing map. Finally, it uses this construction to prove the complexity separation by comparing the quantum solution to the known classical hardness of the problem.
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete, physically relevant demonstration of quantum advantage that is robust to noise and does not rely on unproven complexity assumptions, making it highly relevant for near-term quantum hardware.
